{"content": "# Creating a Google Cloud Compute Engine Instance with an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and Ubuntu 20.04 LTS

Below you’ll find two ways to create the instance:

1. **Using the `gcloud` CLI** – the easiest, most common method.
2. **Using the REST API** – useful if you’re building an automated deployment pipeline.

> **Prerequisites**
> - Google Cloud SDK installed and authenticated (`gcloud auth login`).
> - Compute Engine API enabled for your project.
> - Sufficient GPU quota in the chosen zone.
> - A service account with the `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1` role if you’re calling the REST API.

---

## 1. `gcloud` CLI Command

```bash
# Variables
PROJECT_ID="your-project-id"
ZONE="us-central1-a"          # choose a zone that supports GPUs
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"  # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM
GPU_COUNT=1
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-a6000"
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create $INSTANCE_NAME \
  --project=$PROJECT_ID \
  --zone=$ZONE \
  --machine-type=$MACHINE_TYPE \
  --accelerator=type=$GPU_TYPE,count=$GPU_COUNT \
  --image-family=$IMAGE_FAMILY \
  --image-project=$IMAGE_PROJECT \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
  --tags=http-server,https-server \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform
```

**Notes**:
- `--metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh` is optional; include a script if you need to install drivers or configure the instance after boot.
- `--boot-disk-size` can be adjusted; 100 GB is a good starting point for Ubuntu 20.04.
- `--tags` expose HTTP/HTTPS ports if you plan to run a web server.

## 2. REST API Call

### Endpoint
```
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances
```

### Request Body (JSON)
```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\n# Example: install NVIDIA drivers\napt-get update\napt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Authentication
Use an OAuth 2.0 access token with the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform` scope. Include it in the `Authorization` header:
```
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN
```

### Example `curl` Command
```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/zones/${ZONE}/instances"
```

Replace `${PROJECT_ID}` and `${ZONE}` with your values, and save the JSON body above to `instance.json`.

---

### Quick Checklist
- [ ] Verify GPU quota in the chosen zone.
- [ ] Ensure the `nvidia-a6000` accelerator type is available.
- [ ] Adjust `machineType`, `boot-disk-size`, and `tags` to fit your workload.
- [ ] Test the instance by SSHing in and checking `nvidia-smi`.

Happy GPU computing!", "filename": "create-rtx-a6000-instance.md"}
